2.  26-55711  Recommendation to review and approve applications submitted in response to
  Request for Proposals HSB-2026-003, Continuum of Care Portfolio for New,

  A motion was made by Member McFadzen, seconded by Member Wee, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  8  Boyce, Diles III, McFadzen, Scott, Shuford, Wee, Muñoz, Williams

  • Health Department Staff provided an overview of the CoC Portfolio RFP
  process. HUD is making approximately $4.04 billion available through the FY
  2026 CoC Program Competition.
  • The Long Beach CoC Funding overview was discussed along with the HUD
  funding priorities affecting the local portfolio.
  • The Request for Proposals and evaluation process was discussed, the final

  • The proposals and scores were discussed with the board, the recommended
  RFP project requests for CoC Bonus Reallocation in the amount of

  • The list of project proposals for inclusion was provided along with the

  • A member of the board had questions regarding 1736 Family Crisis Center.

3.  26-55712  Recommendation to review and approve the FY 2026 Long Beach CoC Project
  Performance Scoring Appeals Recommendations.

  A Laid Over was made by Co-Chair Diles III, seconded by Member McFadzen,
  Laid Over. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  8  Boyce, Diles III, McFadzen, Scott, Shuford, Wee, Muñoz, Williams
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 7  Amick, Brown-Shock, Lock, Martins, Rockenbach, Tan, Topolewski

  • Health Department staff Joseph Botelho, provided an overview of the FY
  2026 Continuum of Care (CoC) Project Performance Scoring Appeals
  process and staff recommendations.
  • Staff acknowledged the difficulty of the recommendations and recognized the

  Page 2 of 9

  TUESDAY, AUGUST 4, 2026
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810

  critical role all providers and projects play in serving vulnerable populations.
• Staff noted that this year’s competition is particularly challenging due to new
  federal priorities and the need to maximize funding competitiveness for the
  City of Long Beach.
• Staff clarified that appeals were reviewed based on the approved appeal
  standards:
  o Data calculation errors
  o Incorrect scoring methodology application
  o Eligibility or exemption errors
  o Reallocation amount errors
• Project performance score reports were issued to renewal applicants on July
  14, 2026, and the appeal period closed on July 24, 2026.
• Staff provided a summary of three project scoring appeals:
  o Harbor Interfaith Services: staff recommendation, deny application
  o Interval House-Domestic Violence TH-RRH: staff recommendation,
  approve appeal in part/ deny appeal in part
  o 1736 Family Crisis Center- Domestic Violence: staff recommendation,
  deny application
• Board members asked whether projects denied appeals could be
  reconsidered in the future.
• Staff explained:
  o Providers remain eligible to apply for future funding opportunities
  through local competitions.
  o HUD requires local competition processes for new funding
  opportunities.
  o Projects may be eligible for replacement funding if aligned with future
  funding requirements.
• Board members asked about technical assistance available to providers.
• Staff noted:
  o Technical assistance opportunities are available through HUD and the
  State.
  o Additional technical assistance related to comparable databases and
  data integrity may be explored.
• Board members expressed concern regarding:
  o The impact of funding reductions on long-standing providers.
  o Potential displacement of participants.
  o The need for transition planning and replacement funding strategies.
• Staff emphasized:
  o The scoring and reallocation process is not a reflection of whether a
  provider’s services are valuable.
  o Decisions are based on approved methodologies, HUD requirements,
  and the need to remain competitive under the FY 2026 NOFO.
• Public comment provided from representatives from 1736 Family Crisis
  Center and Harbor Interfaith spoke regarding their appeals.

  • Public commenters expressed concerns regarding:
  o Differences between HMIS and comparable databases used by DV
  providers.
  o Lack of technical assistance related to reporting expectations.
  o Potential impacts on survivors and long-term community services.
  • Providers requested reconsideration of appeal decisions and additional
  support to align reporting practices.
  • Staff shared that potential replacement funding strategies are being
  explored.
  • Staff noted that formal transition plans are still being developed and
  additional information will be brought back to the Board.
  • Board discussed whether to approve appeals individually or collectively.
  • Staff clarified that:
  o Scoring appeals and reallocation recommendations are separate
  processes.
  o Changes to scoring appeals would not automatically resolve
  reallocation impacts.
  • Co-Chair Diles III motioned to table the scoring appeal item for further
  discussion, member McFadzen seconded the motion.
  • The Board moved to approve the motion to table this agenda item.

4.  26-55713  Recommendation to review and approve the FY 2026 Long Beach CoC
  Reallocation recommendations, and hear any appeals.

  A motion was made by Member McFadzen, seconded by Member Shuford, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Boyce, Diles III, McFadzen, Scott, Shuford, Williams
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 2  Wee, Muñoz
  Absent: 7  Amick, Brown-Shock, Lock, Martins, Rockenbach, Tan, Topolewski

  • Health Department staff Joseph Botelho presented the FY 2026 Long Beach
  CoC reallocation recommendations and staff recommendations for four
  appeals received.
  • Staff explained that the reallocation review was based on the approved
  scoring and ranking methodology and reallocation policies and procedures.
  Appeals were limited to data calculation, eligibility, exemption, or reallocation
  amount errors.
  • Staff reviewed the projects identified for reallocation, including voluntary
  portfolio-based reallocations, rapid rehousing projects, chronic
  underutilization, and spend-down reallocations, with the goal of reallocating
  approximately $4.8 million to maximize the CoC's competitiveness for HUD

  Page 4 of 9
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, AUGUST 4, 2026
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810

  funding.
• Four appeals were received from U.S. Vets-Advance/VIP, U.S. Vets-
  CHAMPS, Cabrillo Plaza PHD/SPC 96/99, and 1736 Family Crisis Center.
  o U.S. Vets Advance VIP: Staff recommended denial of the appeal. The
  submitted utilization data included a larger project than the CoC-
  funded scope, and staff determined that the recent consolidation
  exemption was discretionary and did not apply because the projects
  were longstanding.
  o U.S. Vets/CHAMPS: Staff recommended approval of the appeal. The
  project serves veteran families and has four units/seven funded beds.
  Staff determined that the two unoccupied beds were related to family
  composition rather than available vacant beds. The project would
  remain on the priority list, with approximately two-thirds of its funding
  in Tier 1 and the remainder in Tier 2.
  o Cabrillo Plaza PHD: Staff recommended denial of the appeal. Staff
  determined that the one-time funding shift occurred too late in the
  grant term to materially improve the project's spend-down
  performance and that the consolidation exemption was discretionary
  and not applicable.
  o 1736 Family Crisis Center: Staff recommended denial of the appeal.
  Staff determined that the monthly occupancy reports reflected the
  overall facility across multiple funding sources, while the APR data
  reflected participants enrolled in the specific CoC-funded project. Staff
  therefore did not recommend substituting the broader occupancy data
  for the project-level APR data.
• Staff clarified that the reallocation recommendations are based on individual
  reallocation triggers and that a project does not need to meet every trigger to
  be recommended for reallocation.
• Board members discussed concerns regarding the 1736 Family Crisis
  Center appeal, particularly the differences between the APR data and
  monthly occupancy data and whether additional information could be
  considered.
• Staff also discussed potential replacement funding opportunities, including
  transitional housing, supportive services-only projects, and Domestic
  Violence Bonus funding, and emphasized efforts to preserve permanent
  housing.
• Three public commenters from 1736 Family Crisis Center expressed
  concerns regarding the occupancy methodology, the use of APR data, and
  the potential impact of reallocation on domestic violence services and shelter
  capacity.
• Board members discussed the importance of maintaining a consistent and
  objective reallocation methodology while also considering the unique
  circumstances of projects serving domestic violence survivors.
• Staff noted that the approved reallocation policy was established before the

  importance of applying an objective process consistent with HUD
  requirements. Staff advised that changing the methodology would require a
  clear, objective.
  • Staff discussed the possibility of presenting a future funding replacement
  strategy and potential funding opportunities for projects affected by the CoC

5.  26-55714  Recommendation to review and approve the FY 2026 Long Beach CoC Project
  Priority Listing for submission to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban
  Development.

  A motion was made by Member Scott, seconded by Co-Chair Boyce, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Boyce, Diles III, McFadzen, Scott, Shuford, Williams
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 2  Wee, Muñoz
  Absent: 0  None

  • Health Department staff Joseph Botelho reviewed the proposed Tier 1 and
  Tier 2 project rankings, explaining that the ranking methodology reflects the
  previously approved project scoring, reallocation decisions, and funding
  strategy.
  • Staff recommended placing the highest-scoring CoC Bonus project at the top
  of Tier 2, followed by the Domestic Violence (DV) Bonus project. Staff
  explained that the ranking considered both project scores and the likelihood
  of HUD partially funding smaller projects if limited funding remains available.
  • Several new Health Department/Homeless Services Bureau (HSB) project
  proposals, including:
  o An outreach project to strengthen coordination with law enforcement.
  o A family transitional housing project utilizing motel placements for
  crisis housing.
  o A transitional housing project intended to support future housing
  needs as existing funding sources sunset.
  • Staff explained that because the HSB projects are new, they cannot be
  evaluated using historical performance measures. HUD requires all new
  projects to receive a score, and staff assigned a provisional score for ranking
  purposes while requesting Board input on their placement within the priority
  listing.
  • Board members discussed the proposed placement of the HSB projects and

  Page 6 of 9
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, AUGUST 4, 2026
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810

  expressed concerns about assigning new projects a perfect score without
  historical performance data. Members suggested developing a more
  objective scoring process for future competitions.
  • A member of the public expressed concerns regarding the ranking
  methodology and questioned the placement of new HSB projects above
  existing providers with established performance histories.
  • The proposed ranking was intended to maximize available HUD funding and
  ensure that no funding opportunities were left unsubmitted. Staff emphasized
  that the HSB projects could be procured through other entities if awarded
  and that project performance would be evaluated in future funding cycles.
  • Staff further explained that the proposed Domestic Violence Bonus projects
  were ranked lower due to the limited amount of available funding within that
  funding category, not because of project quality or performance.

6.  26-55715  Recommendation to review and approve the Long Beach CoC Recovery-Oriented
  Housing Policy.

  A motion was made by Member Scott, seconded by Member McFadzen, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  8  Boyce, Diles III, McFadzen, Scott, Shuford, Wee, Muñoz, Williams
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 7  Amick, Brown-Shock, Lock, Martins, Rockenbach, Tan, Topolewski

  • Health Department staff Joseph Botelho presented the proposed policy for
  review and approval.
  • The policy was developed in response to new HUD Continuum of Care
  (CoC) requirements. Adoption of the policy will make the CoC eligible to
  receive up to 10 additional points in the annual HUD CoC application,
  strengthening the community's competitiveness for federal funding.
  • Staff clarified that the policy does not:
  o Require all CoC-funded projects to be recovery-oriented or sober
  living programs.
  o Mandate sobriety or participation in treatment.
  o Require termination of participants for first-time drug-related incidents
  or lease violations.
  o Prohibit legally permissible recovery supports, overdose education, or
  other harm reduction services.
  • Staff emphasized that the policy is intended to acknowledge and support
  recovery-oriented housing within the CoC system while ensuring compliance
  with HUD requirements, rather than imposing new restrictions on all housing
  programs.

7.  26-55716  Recommendation to review and approve the Long Beach Coordinated Entry
  System (CES) Prioritization and Transitional Planning Interim Guidance.

  A motion was made by Member McFadzen, seconded by Member Wee, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  8  Boyce, Diles III, McFadzen, Scott, Shuford, Wee, Muñoz, Williams
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 7  Amick, Brown-Shock, Lock, Martins, Rockenbach, Tan, Topolewski

  • Health Department staff Joseph Botelho provided an update and the need
  for a broader tansition process. The interim guidance was developed to
  establish a coordinated process for assisting households facing the
  involuntary loss of housing assistance due to funding exhaustion,
  termination, or reallocation. While the current Emergency Housing Voucher
  (EHV) transition is one example, the guidance is intended to apply broadly to
  any housing program experiencing funding loss.
  • The guidance does not automatically place households into the Housing
  Opportunity Pool, create new eligibility criteria, guarantee placement into
  another housing resource, or prioritize one funding-loss population over
  another. Each household will be assessed individually based on need,
  eligibility, and resource availability.
  • Staff shared that the interim guidance is intended to address immediate
  needs and will later be incorporated into the Long Beach CES Policies and
  Procedures following additional committee review.
  • Staff also provided an update on ongoing efforts to identify additional funding
  sources to support households transitioning from programs experiencing
  funding reductions and emphasized the importance of maintaining continuity
  of housing whenever possible.

8.  26-55717  Recommendation to receive and file an update on outreach and recruitment efforts
  for new Long Beach Continuum of Care (CoC) Board membership seats.

  A motion was made by Member McFadzen, seconded by Member Shuford, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  8  Boyce, Diles III, McFadzen, Scott, Shuford, Wee, Muñoz, Williams
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 7  Amick, Brown-Shock, Lock, Martins, Rockenbach, Tan, Topolewski

  Page 8 of 9
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, AUGUST 4, 2026
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 2:00 PM

  • Health Department staff Joseph Botelho provided an update regarding
  available board seats and the solicitation process. Staff noted that the
  application will be slightly modified to ensure applicants have a strong
  connection to the Long Beach community and are able to fulfill the
  responsibilities and commitment associated with serving on the board.
  • Staff will conduct an attendance review to ensure current board members
  remain committed to serving on the board. Due to ongoing quorum
  challenges, staff emphasized the importance of members understanding and
  fulfilling their attendance and participation responsibilities.

PUBLIC COMMENT

  • No public comments.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

  • Health Department staff member Joseph Botelho provided an update regarding the upcoming
  CoC Board meeting, noting that there will be no Board meeting in September. The Board will
  reconvene in October.
  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan informed the Board that the Health Department will present the
  City's budget to the City Council on the 18th of this month.

ADJOURNMENT

Co-Chair Tamika Boyce adjourned the meeting at 6:05 P.M.
